name: measured
source: Tape-measure + scale readings from the assembled robot, operator, 2026-08-10
notes: The body as BUILT. See docs/operational/picrawler_geometry.md for the full
measured-vs-CAD table and docs/plans-and-designs/picrawler_sim2real_port.md.
FRAME NOTE: the operator measured everything against the HIP2 AXIS, but the sim's
chassis node origin sits at the HIP1 axis (_build_leg anchors hip1 at the chassis
origin's Y, then drops COXA_Z_DROP to hip2).  Every offset below is therefore the
operator's hip2-relative number MINUS coxa_z_drop (0.007):
belly       -19 mm rel hip2  ->  -26 mm rel origin
box seam    +22 mm rel hip2  ->  +15 mm rel origin
stack top   +84 mm rel hip2  ->  +77 mm rel origin
CoG         +15 mm rel hip2  ->   +8 mm rel origin
coxa_z_drop was NOT re-measured -- the operator gave hip2->hip1 as a 32 mm LENGTH,
not its vertical component.  CAD's 7 mm is carried over and is an open item.
Per-segment leg masses are an EQUAL split of the measured 62 g/leg.  The real
distribution is not uniform (coxa carries the hip2 servo, upper the knee servo,
lower is bracket+foot only) but was not measured per segment.  Open item.
CENTRE OF MASS -- +15 mm rel hip2 is the CHASSIS ASSEMBLY's CoG.
Settled 2026-08-10 by the operator's layer description, which is direct observation
and outranks any back-solve.  Chassis layers bottom-to-top: bottom plate, top plate,
RPi, Robot HAT -- with the BATTERY BETWEEN THE PLATES, velcro'd to the underside of
the top plate.  That puts the heaviest single component (~95 g) LOW, inside the base
box, not in the electronics stack.  A layer-by-layer estimate reproduces it:
bottom plate  ~40 g @ -17.5      battery      ~95 g @ +12
4x hip1 servo ~52 g @ -10        top plate    ~40 g @ +22
RPi            45 g @ +30        Robot HAT     30 g @ +45
wiring/screws ~40 g @ +40
=> sum 342 g, CoG +14.9 mm rel hip2  (measured: +15)
In node-origin coords (origin = hip1 = +7 rel hip2): +15 - 7 = +8 mm.
Box split that reproduces it: base ~252 g, electronics ~90 g
(Pi 45 + HAT 30 + wiring ~ 90 g checks out for the top box).
CONSEQUENCE: the WHOLE-ROBOT CoG is then a DERIVED ~+3.9 mm rel hip2, since the
248 g of legs sit at ~-11.4 mm in the standing pose.  _report_geometry() prints
both numbers so the two are never conflated again.
A superseded reading had the +15 mm as the whole-robot CoG, which forced the battery
into the top stack (electronics ~217 g).  The layer description refutes it.
Joint limits and rest poses are deliberately IDENTICAL to cad.json: the servo
envelope is Phase 2 and must not ride along with the geometry lever.
